body.statement:
Let \((X_s,\mathcal G_s)_{s=1}^N\) be a finite real martingale-difference sequence such that \(\sum_{s=1}^N\mathbb E X_s^2=1\) and \(\mathbb E|X_s|^4<\infty\).  There is a universal finite constant \(C\) such that, with \(S_N=\sum_{s=1}^N X_s\) and \(\langle S\rangle_N=\sum_{s=1}^N\mathbb E[X_s^2\mid\mathcal G_{s-1}]\),
\[
 \sup_{x\in\mathbb R}\left|\mathbb P(S_N\le x)-\Phi(x)\right|
 \le C\left\{\sum_{s=1}^N\mathbb E|X_s|^4+
 \mathbb E|\langle S\rangle_N-1|^2\right\}^{1/5}.
\]

source.locator: Theorem 1 specialized to fourth moments; standardized notation is reproduced in Fan and Shao (2018), Introduction, equations (2)--(3)
source.verbatim_statement: Define N_n = sum_{i=1}^n E|X_i|^{2p} + E|<S>_n-1|^p. When p in (1,2], Heyde and Brown proved that there exists a constant C_p depending only on p such that sup_{x in R}|P(S_n <= x)-Phi(x)| <= C_p N_n^{1/(2p+1)}.

upstream.citation: Heyde, C. C. and Brown, B. M. (1970), On the Departure from Normality of a Certain Class of Martingales, Annals of Mathematical Statistics 41, 2161–2165, DOI 10.1214/aoms/1177696722

attestation.note: Lawful open-source verification from Fan and Shao, Self-normalized Cramér type moderate deviations for martingales, arXiv:1712.03667 source TeX, Introduction equations defNn and sfdf, downloaded 2026-09-09. Setting p=2 gives exactly the cited fourth-moment terms and exponent 1/5.
